Customer device verifies the data and formats the financial transaction request before forwarding it.
After forwarding the request to the BUYPASS network node, the customer device starts a 30-second timer.

After receiving approval or decline, the BUYPASS network node forwards the response to the customer's device.

This flow describes an unsuccessful financial transaction (request/response) resulting from a time-out by the customer's host/controller/POS system.
The transaction flow describes single threading (one transaction at a time), but any combination of requests and responses can be in process.
A time-out occurs when the customer's 30-second response interval expires without a response from BUYPASS.
A time-out occurs when a response from BUYPASS is received after the customer's 30-second response interval expires.
If a late response to the original request is received from BUYPASS, the late response is ignored.
After more than three consecutive time-outs in an IP environment, the line to BUYPASS is marked down.
When the line is marked down, send a communications test/health message every 30 seconds until a valid response is received from BUYPASS.
Once a time-out occurs for a device, format a TOR and queue it until the next financial transaction is initiated for that device.
A TOR must be sent from the same device as the original financial transaction request that resulted in the TOR.
When the next financial transaction is initiated from that device, transmit the queued TOR to BUYPASS ahead of the new request.
If no new financial transaction is submitted before end-of-day settlement, the TOR should be sent immediately prior to the settlement request.
When the line is back up, forward off-line transactions to BUYPASS only after a valid response is received for all queued TORs.
Use Sequence Number, Account Number, and dollar amount to match a request with its respective response.
The Sequence Number of a TOR must be the same as the Sequence Number of the financial transaction being reversed.
Each time any financial transaction request is forwarded to BUYPASS, assign a new Sequence Number.
Any response from BUYPASS to a TOR, approval or decline, is considered a valid response and should clear the TOR from the queue.
Continue to send the TOR (subject to health message rules) until a valid response is received.
If no valid response is received after three attempts on each available connection route, log an error in the electronic journal and clear the TOR from the queue.
BUYPASS declines a TOR as an unmatched reversal when BUYPASS has not received the original financial transaction request related to the TOR.
BUYPASS declines a TOR as an unmatched reversal when the original financial transaction has already been reversed.

The specifications support PIN encryption methods DES and 3DES DUKPT.
DUKPT PIN encryption (DUKPT) is the required PIN encryption method for BUYPASS processing.
All personnel are excluded from handling keys in the clear except during initial installation or device adds/modifications.
Personal identification numbers (PINs) and cryptographic keys never appear in the clear.
PINs and cryptographic keys are never retrievable by application programs.
For DUKPT PIN encryption, customer devices and BUYPASS share the same derivation key (DKey).
3DES DUKPT PIN encryption does not require periodic exchange of PIN encryption keys, unlike master session PIN encryption.
A 3DES DUKPT key stored at BUYPASS is used to encrypt a serial number at each PIN pad.
One 3DES DUKPT key exists between BUYPASS and a customer; many PIN pads may share that same key.
A unique serial number is assigned to each PIN pad.
The serial number and its encrypted form (seed key) are inserted in the assigned PIN pad.
The seed key and its corresponding serial number can generate approximately one million unique PIN encryption keys.
Hardware security modules must be used to encrypt all PINs, following ANSI PIN management standards.
Transmission of a PIN among interface participants must use DES-encrypted ANSI PIN blocks.
To encrypt a PIN block for transmission to BUYPASS, required data are the card PAN, cardholder PIN, and generated KPE.
Point-of-entry device prompts for a 4- to 12-digit PIN using a secure PIN pad.
At point-of-entry, the PIN is encrypted with the generated KPE.
The encrypted PIN block and the KSN are sent to the customer's host system for forwarding to BUYPASS.
DES DUKPT must be defined.
BUYPASS retrieves the customer's 3DES DUKPT key from its database; the key is encrypted under the BUYPASS master file key in the BUYPASS HSM.
Encrypted PIN block, PAN, KSN, and 3DES DUKPT key are passed to BUYPASS HSM and translated into a new translated encrypted PIN block using the BUYPASS master key.
In the BUYPASS HSM, the encrypted PIN block is translated to a new translated PIN block using the network's interchange working key.
The encrypted PIN is transmitted to the network host system.
The pathway terminal configuration for the PIN pad value must be defined for 3DES DUKPT.
At the Bank FIID level the key representation for 3DES DUKPT must be defined.

DUKPT uses DKey and KSN to generate a unique PIN encryption key for every transaction at a PIN pad.
The DKey is comprised of two 16-hexadecimal (HEX) character halves that are concatenated.
The two DKey halves are loaded onto the processor's host and associated with a given customer base.
BUYPASS supports 2-part and 3-part keys.
The KSN is a 20-byte HEX field.
During initialization, the DKey and an initial key sequence number (IKSN) are used to create the base PIN encryption key.
Future PIN encryption keys for any PIN entry device are derived from the base PIN encryption key.
The IKSN is 20 bytes and the right-most 4 bytes (Transaction Counter) must be initialized to 0's.
Each PIN-based transaction causes the KSN to increment, changing the key at the PIN pad each time.
Because the same DKey is stored on the host and used in PIN pad injection, the host can derive the PIN block in each transaction.
The initial value of a 20-byte IKSN must follow the format PPPPXXXXXXXXXXEZ0000.
In IKSN format, PPPP represents HEX characters (F's).
In IKSN format, XXXXXXXXXX represents any 10-byte HEX character string.
In IKSN format, E represents any even HEX character (e.g., 0, 2, C, E).
In IKSN format, Z represents zero.
In IKSN format, 0000 represents the Transaction Counter value.
The Transaction Counter can be manually included in the IKSN or programmatically concatenated by vendor software such as MKIXOR.
The block must be at least 4 digits and no greater than 12 digits in length.
A test key is used for certifications; clear key components are given for PIN pad injection along with the KSN.
Overall left and right halves of the clear key components are given.
The encrypted PIN block is constructed from the combination of the entered PIN and PAN fields.
The block must be at least 4 digits and no greater than 12 digits in length.
A digit is a 4-bit binary number with value 0-15 (0-F).
PIN field control nibble C is always zero.
PIN field length nibble L is the length of entered PIN as a 4-bit binary number (4-12).
Entered PIN digits N are left aligned, including any leading zeros.
Pad digits F are (14-L) digits of 1111 (F).
Calculate the PAN field from Track 2 by dropping the check digit prior to the '=' separator.
Use the remaining right-most 12 digits after dropping the check digit to populate P digits.
PAN field control digits C are always zero.
The last digit of the PAN is considered a check digit whether it is or not.
The 16-byte PIN block in field no. 8 of the Standard Message Segment is followed by the KSN.

BUYPASS does not provide an electronic journal feature; customers can design, create, and implement one.

Local totals should accumulate transactions in the electronic journal and include authorization only transactions.

If no entries are present in the electronic journal, a 'no entries' message displays and the device returns to the idle prompt.
If entries are present, a message displays indicating there are entries and a designated key enables proceeding to subsequent prompts.

ENTER ACCOUNT NUMBER: enter a partial account number to display a list of accounts beginning with this number.

If a match is found, the transaction(s) display on the device screen; a designated key advances one transaction at a time.
When scrolling electronic journal entries, the most recent entry displays first.
Electronic Journal Field 1 must contain a minimum of the first 16 positions of the account number.
In Electronic Journal Field 2, xx is the day and hh:mm is the time the transaction was performed.
In Electronic Journal Field 2, zzz is the transaction sequence number, where 1 represents the oldest transaction.

When requesting host totals, the device displays a prompt for entering a password and date.

Host totals are accessed by entering a 6-digit Totals Date code (Element No. 105).
BUYPASS maintains two sets of daily totals for each merchant: shift totals and settlement totals.
Shift totals accumulate from work shift to work shift and are scratch totals that do not affect settlement.
Shift totals can accumulate beyond a merchant's cut time.
Shift totals requests can be read only or read and reset.
For a Read Only Total Request, enter Totals Date code 111111 in the device date field.
Totals Date code 111111 enables viewing shift totals without resetting shift total amounts to zero.
For Totals Date code 111111, BUYPASS returns host shift totals for transactions since the last shift cut.
For a Read and Reset Total Request, enter Totals Date code 999999 in the device date field.
Totals Date code 999999 enables viewing shift totals and resetting shift total amounts to zero.
For Totals Date code 999999, BUYPASS ends the current shift and resets merchant shift totals to zero.
If shift totals are not requested at shift end, totals continue to accumulate until a 999999 request is made.
Shift totals are available until the first transaction in a new shift has been completed.
Shift totals can be retrieved from the most recently completed shift.
Settlement totals accumulate over a 24-hour period and are totaled once a day.
Settlement time (cut time) is determined by the merchant.
A merchant may cut totals before the default settlement time; such a merchant is a variable-cut merchant.
Settlement totals can be requested as read only or read and cut.
Business day totals can be requested as read only for current, previous, or the business day before the previous.
For read-only settlement totals, enter the desired settlement date in format MMDDYY in the device date field.
Using Totals Date code MMDDYY returns totals for transactions that settled on the specified date.
Read-only request with a specific date allows viewing totals without resetting BUYPASS settlement total amounts to zero.
Settlement date is when transactions actually settle; it may not coincide with BUYPASS end-of-business day.
In most cases, to retrieve totals for a current business day, request totals using settlement date equal to business day plus one day.
BUYPASS groups transactions done in the end-of-business 24-hour period and totals them, but does not run settlement until 2:00 p.m.
If merchant end-of-day is 6:00 p.m., transactions for that day settle at 2:00 p.m. on the following day.
Read and cut settlement totals request option can be used only by variable-cut merchants.
To request totals for the current settlement date as read and cut, enter Totals Date code 222222 in the device date field.
Entering 222222 allows a variable-cut merchant to close its business day before the predetermined cut time in the BUYPASS merchant profile.
If the merchant does not request read and cut totals, BUYPASS automatically closes the business day at the designated cut time.
Transactions performed after close of business are included in the next business day's totals.
In controller-based automated fuel pump environments, the controller should connect to BUYPASS 30 minutes before cut time and forward all queued trailer transactions.
Forwarding queued trailer transactions before cut time ensures authorization-only/preauthorization pairs are captured on the same business day.
After transmitting all trailer transactions, the controller completes a read and cut total request using Totals Date code 222222.
If a read and cut total request is not made, BUYPASS automatically closes the merchant's business day at designated cut time.
If a device supports table loads from BUYPASS, receiving Card Type (Element No. 14) value "164" enables Auto Close in the device.
To request current business day read-only settlement totals, enter Totals Date code 333333 in the device date field.
Using Totals Date code 333333 produces the same result as the Read Only Settlement Totals Request described in section 9.3.2.1.
To request previous business day read-only settlement totals, enter Totals Date code 444444 in the device date field.
Calendar days may elapse between business days; e.g., a Monday request can return totals for the previous Friday if no weekend transactions occurred.
To request totals for the business day before the previous business day, enter Totals Date code 555555 in the device date field.
Calendar days may elapse between business days; e.g., a Monday request can return totals for the previous Thursday if no weekend transactions occurred.

If store retains account info from original attempt, remaining information can be entered at controller level or directly into the lane device.

Receipt must print whether transaction is Food Stamp or Cash Benefit, and indicate the type of transaction attempted.
Clerk ID is an optional receipt requirement; it may be retrieved or prompted for and printed on the receipt.

For Food Stamp Electronic Voucher transactions only, the manually entered Voucher Number must appear on the receipt.
Food stamp dollar amount must be printed on a Food Stamp transaction receipt.
Cash benefit dollar amount(s) must be printed on a Cash Benefit transaction receipt.
Transaction amounts must be broken down for purchases versus cash back and include a total if both amounts were entered.
For both Food Stamp and Cash Benefit transactions, the ending balance must be printed on the receipt.
Beginning EBT balance may be printed by calculating it from ending balance and transaction amount.
EBT authorizers may return food stamp balance only, cash benefit balance only, or both balances.
If a particular balance is not returned, do not print a balance of zero; omit the (text truncated).
Balances of zero dollars should be printed only when zero is actually returned as the balance from the authorizer.
Approval Number and the message from the transaction response must be printed on receipts for all approved EBT transactions.
When a PIN is entered, a PIN USED message prints on the transaction receipt.
All declined transactions must print a receipt, and the reason for the decline must be indicated on the receipt.

These specifications do not support Return transactions.
The following nonfinancial transaction types are supported for eWIC: eWIC Authorization (Benefits Inquiry), Authorization Cancellation, and Balance Inquiry.
If there is a time-out or the eWIC client cancels the order, an eWIC Authorization Cancellation transaction is required.
eWIC Authorization (Benefits Inquiry) is initiated by card swipe, then PIN entry, then device sends an Authorization Request to BUYPASS for processing and response forwarding.
eWIC Authorization Cancellation is initiated by card swipe and PIN entry; device sends Cancellation Request to BUYPASS; BUYPASS processes and forwards Cancellation Response.
For eWIC Authorization Cancellation, the device displays/prints the eWIC account balance information from the Response.
eWIC Balance Inquiry is initiated by card swipe and PIN entry; device sends Balance Inquiry Request to BUYPASS; BUYPASS processes and forwards Balance Inquiry Response.
For eWIC Balance Inquiry, the device displays/prints the eWIC account balance information from the Response.
eWIC Authorization (Benefits Inquiry) enables querying the eWIC host for eWIC-approved product list and account balance information.
eWIC Balance Inquiry enables querying the eWIC host for remaining eWIC account balance information.
The eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Response must be received by the device.
The following nonfinancial transaction types are supported for eWIC: eWIC Purchase Completion; eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void.
If there is a time-out or the eWIC client cancels the order, an eWIC Authorization Cancellation transaction is required.
eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void reverses/voids effects at the eWIC host when an eWIC Purchase Response is not received or is received late at the POS device.
eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void must be completed and its Response received before any additional eWIC transactions can be sent from the originating device.
If the eWIC host responds to the Purchase Reversal/Void Request, the transaction is considered processed regardless of the Response Code.
If no Purchase Reversal/Void Response is received, the Merchant must repeat the process until a Response is received.
eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void is initiated when an eWIC Purchase Response is received late or when a time-out situation exists.
eWIC Voucher Clear is an optional transaction.
eWIC Voucher Clear settles a previously authorized eWIC Voucher by electronically submitting phone approvals during a device/BUYPASS/eWIC host outage.
This transaction is initiated when the clerk determines the device/BUYPASS/eWIC host is offline.
If the authorization center declines the transaction, the eWIC client leaves.
If the authorization center approves the transaction, it provides an eWIC Approval Number and the clerk issues a paper eWIC Voucher.
The paper eWIC Voucher contains: eWIC Voucher Number, eWIC Account Number, eWIC Approval Number, and eWIC Transaction Amount.
Voucher information must be electronically submitted to the eWIC host within the Merchant's specified time limit for the Merchant to receive payment.
Using the Merchant copy of the voucher, the clerk keys the voucher information into the device together with any applicable manufacturer/cents-off discount coupon amounts.
The device sends an eWIC Voucher Clear Request to BUYPASS; BUYPASS processes it and sends an eWIC Voucher Clear Response to the device.
The device displays/prints the eWIC information from the eWIC Voucher Clear Response.

A stored value card cannot be used for transactions until it has been activated.
There are three activation methods: without a device; using a device with predefined limit; using a device with customer-defined limit (issuer-activated).
Activation without using a device requires receipt by the vendor of a fulfillment letter confirming shipment to the client.
For device activation with a predefined limit, the package is activated by swiping through the card reader of an indoor device.
If the card's magnetic stripe is invalid during predefined-limit activation, the entire package is discarded and the process repeated with a new package.
If an "approved" Response is received for predefined-limit activation, the card is active and ready to use up to the predefined monetary limit.
For customer-defined value activation, the card is activated by swiping through a card reader and entering the activation amount at an indoor device.
If an "approved" Response is received for customer-defined value activation, the card is active and ready to use up to the defined monetary limit.
The card can be used until its monetary limit is exhausted.
Clients can determine whether purchases can be made under a specific amount (for example, $1.00).
If an activated card is not used within the time frame established by its authorizer, it can be deactivated at any participating client's devices.

For SVC processing, the following point-of-sale transactions are supported: Purchase/Capture, Purchase Reversal, Authorization Only, Authorization Only Reversal, Merchandise Return, Activation, Deactivation, Recharge/Issue Card, Balance Merge, Replace Card, Balance Inquiry, Cancellation, Cancellation (Time-out Reversal).
For SVC processing, the following customer-activated transactions are supported: Purchase/Capture, Authorization Only, Authorization Only Reversal, Cancellation (Time-out Reversal).
For InComm, the following additional transaction type is supported: Account Verification (Preauthorization Activation).
In a Purchase/Capture transaction, if an approved response is received, the issuer deducts the purchase amount from the card balance; otherwise, a declined response is sent to the device.
A Purchase Reversal transaction adds the transaction amount to the card's balance.
For Purchase Reversal, the amount must be the exact amount of a previous SVC transaction, and the previous transaction must have been done in the same business day.
For Purchase Reversal, the POS device must subtract the amount from the SVC bucket and subtract this transaction from the SVC quantity.
An Authorization Only transaction places a lock on the card, and the client decides the duration of the lock.
The Authorization Only Response contains the card's balance and the authorization number.
Authorization Only Reversal is used if the device fails, or a communication problem occurs after the device receives an approved Authorization Only Response.
Authorization Only Reversal has an amount previously set by the client; when received, the card issuer unlocks the SVC account.
A Merchandise Return transaction adds the given amount to the card's balance.
For Merchandise Return, the POS device must subtract the amount from the SVC bucket and add this transaction to the SVC quantity.
After a successful Activation Transaction, charges can be made against the SVC account.

After successful Deactivation, account number can be closed and charges can no longer be made, depending on client configuration.

For First Data Premium Gift Card Cash Out, amount used to bring balance to $0.00 is returned in response Approved Amount field.
After successful Cash Out, account can remain open with balance $0.00, depending on client configuration.

Supported loyalty advice functions for loyalty card processing include Add account, Coupon redemption, Expiration date update, Account inquiry, Points redemption, Reversal of coupon redeem, Reversal of points redeemed, and Sale update.
Add account is used to add a new loyalty account to the loyalty host from a POS device.
For Add account, the clerk swipes a new loyalty card and enters the customer's street number and telephone number.
Coupon redemption is used to redeem coupons for payment from a POS device.
For Coupon redemption, clerk swipes the loyalty card or manually keys the loyalty account number and enters Coupon ID and Coupon Amount.
If the loyalty card is not available, in lieu of the Loyalty Account Number, the clerk enters both the consumer's street number and telephone number.
Expiration date update is used to update the expiration date of an account on the loyalty host from a POS device.
For Expiration date update, clerk swipes the loyalty card or manually keys the account number.
If the loyalty card is not available, in lieu of the Loyalty Account Number, the clerk enters both the consumer's street number and telephone number.
For Expiration date update, the host extends the loyalty account for a predefined amount of time.
Account inquiry is used to inquire about the status of a loyalty account from a POS device.
For Account inquiry, clerk swipes the loyalty card or manually keys the account number.
If the loyalty card is not available, in lieu of the Loyalty Account Number, the clerk enters both the consumer's street number and telephone number.
For Account inquiry, the host returns the Loyalty Print Data in the response.
For Account inquiry, the data returned to the device is a pre-programmed message maintained by the merchant at the loyalty host.
Points redemption is used to redeem points for payment from a POS device.
For Points redemption, clerk swipes the loyalty card or manually keys the Loyalty Account Number and enters the number of points to redeem for payment.
If the loyalty card is not available, in lieu of the Loyalty Account Number, the clerk enters both the consumer's street number and telephone number.
Reversal of coupon redeem is used to reverse coupons redeemed on a previously approved coupon redemption transaction from a POS device.
For Reversal of coupon redeem, clerk swipes the loyalty card or manually keys the account number and enters Coupon ID, Coupon Amount, and approval number of the previous receipt.
If the loyalty card is not available, in lieu of the Loyalty Account Number, the clerk enters both the consumer's street number and telephone number.
Reversal of points redeemed is used to reverse points redeemed on a previously approved point redemption transaction from a POS device.
For Reversal of points redeemed, clerk swipes the loyalty card or manually keys the account number and enters the point amount and approval number of the previous receipt.
If the loyalty card is not available, in lieu of the Loyalty Account Number, the clerk enters both the consumer's street number and telephone number.
Sale update is listed as a supported loyalty advice function, but no behavior is described on this page.
A transaction is used to update the loyalty host with noncredit card sale data for a loyalty account from a POS device.
The clerk swipes the loyalty card or manually keys the Loyalty Account Number and enters the amount of the noncredit card or cash sale.
If the loyalty card is not available, the clerk enters both the consumer's street number and telephone number in lieu of the Loyalty Account Number.
Account update is used to update street address and phone number information on a loyalty account from a POS device.
For account update, the clerk swipes the loyalty card and must enter both the new street number and new telephone number.
Totals Report, Loyalty is used to request a summary of all loyalty transactions and subtotal by card number.
Selecting the totals menu option from the loyalty menu initiates a request to the loyalty host; the host returns the totals report for the device to print.
Credit card receipt requirements in section 10.1.7 also apply to loyalty cards.
Any additional loyalty card information received by the device (per Appendix K/Table 008/Table 010) is printed on the loyalty card receipt.
Vendors who support their own applications do not use software update processing.
Software update processing uses an automated request by an active device for a full application download from BUYPASS-supported device management.
A bit is set on the merchant profile at BUYPASS indicating the device must request a DLL.
When the merchant profile bit indicates a DLL is required, BUYPASS sends Download Indicator = 1 in the next transaction response.
After receiving Download Indicator = 1, the device sends a Table Load request to BUYPASS.
In response to a Table Load request, BUYPASS sends Software Dial Load Data Segment and Software IP Load Data Segment.
Device stores New Software Version, Software Terminal Record ID, Software Load Phone Number or Software Load IP/URL Address, Software Load Request Date, and Software Load Request Time.
At the designated date and time, the device dials the Software Load Phone Number/Software Load IP/URL Address and requests a full application load.
Upon completion of the full application load, the device dials BUYPASS and requests a Table Load.
BUYPASS responds to the post-load Table Load request by sending the Table Load without requiring the merchant profile bit to be set.
The device can attempt to request the automated full application load a maximum of three times.
If the load request to Software Load Phone Number/Software Load IP/URL Address is unsuccessful, the device prints the "decline" message.
Electronic Mail Retrieval uses an Electronic Mail Request with Prompt Code 981.
Retrieval of proprietary card data uses an Electronic Mail Request with Prompt Code 996.

Electronic Mail Submission uses an Electronic Mail Request with Prompt Code 995.
The Electronic Mail Request for submission contains up to 217 bytes of data.
BUYPASS sends an Electronic Mail Response to confirm receipt of the Electronic Mail Request.
For submission, the data is stored at BUYPASS.
Data sent to BUYPASS for retrieval is stored until transmission to the client's store POS device.

Check with your First Data Certification Representative for availability of the Payment Token processing feature.
Payment token replaces the Primary Account Number (PAN) with a token number for device and/or e-commerce transactions.
Payment token issuance is performed by a token vault that generates and stores the payment token and associated PAN.
The operator of the token vault is referred to as the token service provider.
The token requestor is typically an acquirer, merchant, or digital wallet provider using tokens to replace PAN in databases and processing.
Payment processes needing token support may include authorization, capture, clearing, and exception processing.
For additional payment tokenization terminology information, refer to Appendix O (Payment Tokenization Terminologies).
Payment Token ranges will be in the existing ranges of the relevant card brand.
Payment Tokenization replaces the Primary Account Number (PAN) with a token number for device and/or eCommerce payment transactions.
Payment Tokens are mapped to the PAN, leveraging existing payments infrastructure and messaging formats for authorization and processing.
The Payment Token will be used for the entire life-cycle of the transaction for all card brands.
EMVCo manages the Payment Token Standard.
A payment token transaction replaces the actual card PAN with an association payment token.
Payment token transactions may occur for NFC transactions when the NFC device sends a Payment Token instead of the actual card number.
Payment token transactions may occur for eCommerce transactions with security data containing token cryptogram, like VPAS or UCAF.
Payment token transactions may occur for card-on-file where the initial transaction contains the token with valid cryptogram and may be saved for subsequent transactions.
For NFC in-person purchase, merchant submits authorization as a contactless transaction exactly as they do today.
For mobile app (in app) eCommerce, merchant sends authorization request with appropriate data including the cryptogram.
For Mobile App (In App) eCommerce subsequent token transactions, specific field requirements must be included in the authorization request to avoid decline.
Specific field requirements for subsequent token-transaction authorizations vary by card brand.
In Card On File (COF), the payment token provided by the card brand replaces the PAN stored at the merchant.
A stored credential includes an account number or payment token stored by merchant/agent/payment facilitator/staged digital wallet operator for future transactions.
A credential is not considered a stored credential when card details are stored to complete a single transaction.
A credential is not considered a stored credential when card details are stored to complete multiple authorizations related to the initial transaction (e.g., incremental transactions).
A Cardholder-Initiated Transaction (CIT) is any transaction where the cardholder actively participates, in-store, online checkout, or a subsequent stored credential transaction.
A Merchant-Initiated Transaction (MIT) is a subsequent transaction with already stored credentials without the cardholder’s active engagement, based on prior consent.
Once credentials are shared for storage at a merchant location/website, standing instruction MITs are considered subsequent transactions.
A separate transaction to buy a different item again using the same card at the same merchant location/website is considered a subsequent transaction (standing instruction MIT).
A recurring transaction associated with the original transaction is considered a subsequent transaction (standing instruction MIT).
An installment transaction associated with the original transaction is considered a subsequent transaction (standing instruction MIT).
Installments must be sent for Discover.
Use cases listed are not exhaustive; they describe only some common stored credential scenarios.
When Merchant Name is sent from a Third Party Payment Providor, the underlying merchant name field must also be present.
Merchant Name must be formatted as: third party installment provider name + '*' + underlying retailer name.
SIC Information with MCC/SIC of underlying retailer of a third-party payment provider for Installments must be sent for Discover.
MIT/CIT category and subcategory data (Table 56 Sub Table 09) is used for MasterCard card type.

For first-time storing credentials (CIT), include DE111 Table 32 Sub table 08 with value 'I' (Initial).
For MasterCard card type in CIT, merchant needs to send MIT/CIT category and subcategory data with valid value as applicable.

Transaction Attribute Sequence uses value 'C' to indicate Credential on File.

There are four categories of Common AIDs: Visa Common AID, US Maestro AID, DNA Shared Debit AID, Discover Common AID.
Any of the Common AIDs may be used in processing a Common AID transaction.
Visa and US Maestro Common AID transactions should be submitted as 'credit / 0100 / Dual message' requests.
If First Data receives a credit request with cashback for Visa or US Maestro Common AID, it will route it (except Discover) to a single message debit network.
Discover supports cashback on credit requests; First Data does not support cashback for Visa or MasterCard credit/Signature Debit transactions.
DNA Shared Debit AID is limited to 'debit / 0200 / single message' networks; submit DNA Shared Debit AID as debit/0200/single message requests.
If First Data receives a debit request with cashback for DNA Shared Debit AID, it will route the transaction to a 'single message' debit network.

POS devices that support EMV PIN must support both online PIN and offline PIN processing.
POS devices processing chip-initiated credit and signature debit must be capable to submit a PIN in the authorization request.
Online PIN is electronically sent to and validated by the card issuer.
Offline PIN is matched to an application on the EMV chip card; authorization request may still be sent to the issuer.
In a traditional PIN Debit transaction, PIN field is mandatory and must contain either a PIN or all F's for offline PIN.
If the mandatory PIN field is not sent as PIN or all F's (offline PIN), the transaction will decline as "invalid transaction".
In a credit/signature debit transaction, a PIN of all F's is not required because PINs are optional.
Fallback is acceptance of chip cards via magnetic-stripe processing at a chip-capable device.
If a chip card is presented at a chip-capable terminal and chip transaction cannot be performed, merchant may process as magnetic stripe (swipe).
Fallback transactions must be properly identified as such in the authorization message.
A fallback will occur whenever an EMV certified solution cannot read or obtain a viable matching AID.
If device is EMV enabled, card is chip, and card is swiped, always send Fallback Entry Mode '80' (or spec equivalent).
If card is not chip or device is not chip capable and card is swiped, send MSR Entry Mode '90' (or spec equivalent).
